description: What NTFS's journal, $LogFile, says of whether Windows left its volume in use, read from its first bytes as ntfs-3g reads them (libntfs-3g/logfile.c): restart pages, RSTR or CHKD, searched at 0 and at each power of two from 512 that a read reached, the restart page header, its restart area and its client array checked, the update sequence applied; of two, the newer by LSN. empty: no block searched is anything but 0xFF. clean: no client in use, or RESTART_VOLUME_IS_CLEAN (0x0002) set. unclean: a client in use and that flag clear. version-2: clean, of version 2.0, which ntfs-3g refuses to mount read-write as Windows may keep its metadata cached. invalid: no restart page that holds, the newer one torn, or a $LogFile too small: nothing proves it clean. size is the file's size; length how many of its first bytes a read gave: fill, 00 when not given, then each of bytes in its order, zeros or hex.

cases.note: empty: 0xFF where every restart page may be, as mkntfs makes it and the drivers of Linux leave it
zeros: no restart page, and not empty
clean 1.1: its client in use, RESTART_VOLUME_IS_CLEAN set, as a full shutdown of Windows leaves it
clean 1.1: no client in use
unclean 1.1: a client in use and the flag clear, as ntfs-3g's 'unclean file system (0, 0)'
unclean 2.0, as Windows 8 and later leave a volume they keep mounted
clean 2.0: Windows may keep its metadata cached, which ntfs-3g refuses to mount read-write
the second page newer and clean, the first unclean: the newer counts
the first page newer and clean, the second unclean
the first page newer and unclean, the second clean
the same LSN on both: the first counts
the newer page torn in its sixth sector, its restart area whole in the first: no proof of a clean journal
a torn page older than a whole one: the whole one counts
a torn page whose restart area runs past the first sector is no restart page
the first page with an update sequence of the wrong count, the second unclean
both pages with an update sequence of the wrong count
